label: text
text: With reference to the offer of new shares dated the 10th June, 1925 (made to existing shareholders of the Company) by the terms of which the sum of $30 per share was to be paid on or before the 15th July, 1925, and the sum of $30 per share on or before the 15th October, 1925, the Directors have decided that as regards those shareholders (having a registered address in the Far East) who do not feel themselves (owing to present circumstances) in a position to accept the Company's offer on or before the 15th July, 1925, a further opportunity shall be given to them to take up the new shares.

label: text
text: Such shareholders may accordingly take up the new shares on or before the 15th day of September before the 15th day of September, 1925, and may pay the first instalment of $30 per new share on or before that date. They will, however, be required to pay interest at 6 per cent. per annum on the amount of such first instalment from the 15th day of July, 1925, until the date of payment.

label: text
text: The second instalment of $30 per share will be payable not later than the 15th December, 1925, and interest upon it will be payable from the 15th October, 1925, at the rate of 6 per cent. per annum until the date of payment.

label: text
text: This notice will not affect those shareholders who accept or have accepted the original offer and who make payment on the dates originally fixed i.e. as regards the first instalment on or before the 15th July, 1925, and as regards the second instalment on or before the 15th October, 1925.

label: text
text: BRITISH AND ARGENTINE GOODWILL

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Buenos Aires, August 18.
The Prince of Wales was noisily welcomed, with crashing salutes by the Argentinian warships, the whistles of a score of vessels in the harbour, the disone of aeroplanes circling overhead, and shouts of welcome from the packed main street, through which the Prince slowly drove amid a shower of flowers; not to mention the clicking of the inevitable cameras and kinematographs.

label: text
text: The city in the evening was brilliantly illuminated. The Prince was entertained to a banquet at Government House, which was followed by a tattoo.

label: text
text: "I at ter.

label: text
text: A gala banquet at the Government Palace was numerously attended, including the Government and civic authorities, diplomas and other prominent persons.

label: text
text: President: Alvarez toasting the Prince of Wales said that the Prince's visit afforded a wonderful opportunity to draw closer the historic bonds of Anglo-Argentine amity.

label: text
text: The Prince in reply said that South Africa and Argentina were both new hands with different problems to solve, but both were working confidently for human progress and civilisation. He was sure Aglo-Argentine friendship and commercial intercourse would be prolonged indefinitely. President Alvour called a message of good will to King George.

label: paragraph_title
text: “FURTHER EVILS.”

label: text
text: CHINESE AND THE MIXED COURT.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
London, August 18,
The Chinese Minister of Justice has telegraphed to Mr. Ramsay Macdonald, Mr. Bertrand Russell Mr. H. G. Wells, Mr. Bernard Shaw and others declaring interalia that the Shanghai Mixed Court has no legal foundation and that it is due to its existence that the local Chinese Court is prevented from holding an judicial enquiry into the shooting affair. The continued existence of the Mixed Court will constitute further evils that are bound to breed troubles.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOW TO GET ON.

label: text
text: HOME SECRETARY ON IDEALS FOR YOUTH.

label: text
text: Sir William Joynson-Hicks, the Home Secretary, presented the prizes at the speech day at Dean Close School, Cheltenham, and subsequently addressed the boys, Chair parents, and friends.

label: text
text: There is a demand for good me! today just as great as ever there was," declared Sir William. "There is an insistent demand for men.

label: text
text: every rank, in every business, in every profession; men who can be depended upon, men who have a foundation of character, and, above all else, men who are prepared to work." (Cheers.)

label: text
text: Sir William said that he was quite cravined that the modern idea of working seven or eight hours a day would do nothing more than keep men in the middle rut of life, and they would never get out of it. He urged the boys not to slouch through the last two or three years of school life, wondering in a vague sort of way what they were going to do, and imagining that the "Governor" or the "Old Bean", would decide for them, and do what was best. Boys should think for themselves what they were best capable of, and what line of life would be best for themselves and for the country. He warned them against shifting and drifting from one profession to another.

label: text
text: There are more vacancies for a ten-thousand-a-year man than there are for a two-pound-a-week man, because there are practically no vacancies for the latter. But the big jobs were not for the man who would only work the ordinary hours and was content with the ordinary trade union wages. Business people wanted the young man who was not hide-bound, the man who would devote his whole soul to his work, and that was the man it was so difficult to get.

label: text
text: Emphasising the necessity for character, Sir William remarked: "It is no use having a first-class brain if there is a second-class character behind it. Speaking as a business man, I think a first-class character and a second-class brain will carry you a good deal further than a first-class brain and a second-class character." (Cheers).

label: text

label: text
text: Sir Robert Horne, M.P., speaking at an East Lothian Unionist Fête at Gosford Grounds, Haddingtonshire, said the uprisings in Shanghai were due to the persistent and assiduous efforts made by the Soviet Government of Russia against, etabl Government in every part of the world. The Soviet recognised that the chief opponent and the greatest obstruction to the theory of Communistic Government was Great Britain. If they could get rid of the influence of Great Britain in the world, they would have done more than by any other effort to establish their hateful disastrous theories throughout the whole world.

label: text
text: HORNE'S CONFIDIN OUR POLICY.

label: text
text: "They have been striving now," said Sir Robert, "for the last four years in the face of very solemn obligations under a Treaty, which I made with them myself to upset our Government in India, and to set the whole of the East aflame. Happily, they have entirely failed, but in China they have found elements which are more easy to work upon, and to-day you find the ministers of this great Soviet Republic of Russia boasting of the attack which they are making against our interests in China, and asserting that the disturbances that we have already seen are only a poor rehearsal of the massacres which they hope to see in the future.

label: text
text: Said Sandy: "If you throw a penny out of the carriage window whenever you are crossing a river, you will never be in a rail-

label: text
text:
It is for us to see that the defence of our citizens there is made secure. We can thank Godt o-day that we have a Government in power with a proper appreciation of the situation and we can thank Heaven, too, for our knowledge that whatever happens, no prejudice in favour of this disastrous system which has destroyed Russia will prevent the Government taking all the adequate means in their power for the safety of our British fellow subjects.
Urging the need for trade development, Sir Robert said he welcomed the chance of peace in Europe which had been brought nearer by the great Pact which Mr. Austen Chamberlain had been endeavouring to make with other countries. The greatest hope of the country for the future was in the great Dominions and possessions which they enjoyed in other parts of the world. It was for them to encourage the union of Great Britain in political and commercial matters.
